items.summary: USGS Groundwater-Depth Dataset Processing Workflow v1.0.0 is the archived software release of the public processing workflow developed to construct the Version 1.0 quality-controlled daily groundwater-depth dataset derived from the U.S. Geological Survey National Water Information System (USGS NWIS). The workflow processes USGS parameter 72019 (depth to water below land surface), daily mean statistic 00003, Approved source values, and wells classified with USGS code U (Unconfined single aquifer). It implements normalization and quality control, temporal continuity assessment, segmentation of fragmented monitoring histories, development and reserved-validation masking, PCHIP reconstruction of short internal gaps, and final dataset export with explicit source/interpolation provenance. The frozen workflow uses a minimum retained span of 10 years, a maximum internal missing-gap threshold of 30 days, PCHIP interpolation without extrapolation, exactly 50 development masks and 20 reserved-validation masks per required gap length where applicable, and a pooled RMSE acceptance threshold of 0.20 m at every required masking length. Segment selection is fixed before reserved validation, and no alternative segment is substituted after a reserved-validation failure. The software supported construction of a final dataset containing 331 monitoring wells and 2,374,112 daily values, including 2,357,801 retained USGS source values and 16,311 PCHIP-reconstructed values. The associated scientific dataset is archived separately on Zenodo and is not distributed as part of this software record. This repository is a public adaptation of the research workflow with portable paths and reproducibility documentation. The scientific processing criteria and numerical methods of the frozen Version 1.0 workflow are preserved. Source repository: https://github.com/joelgarciapazos/usgs-groundwater-processing Release: v1.0.0

items.summary: Many LLM agents maintain external persistent memory and derive additional state from past interactions, such as summaries. Deleting an original memory record therefore need not remove information carried by its descendants. We introduce AfterDeleteBench, a controlled behavioral audit for this failure mode in fixed-weight LLM agents. For each synthetic secret, we compare an exposed-then-deleted agent with an otherwise matched agent that was never exposed to the secret, allowing post-deletion recovery to be attributed to the original exposure. In our primary setting, a single query recovers the deleted secret from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in roughly two thirds of cases, while matched never-exposed controls have zero recovery. Crucially, recovery does not require a surviving verbatim copy: when the complete secret string is absent and only separately stored components remain under a public composition rule, exact reconstruction succeeds in 62-99% of cases across Qwen, Mistral, and Phi-3. We also show that the response interface is part of the measurement system: target-bearing replies can be scored as failures when the requested format and parser are misaligned. Finally, we separate reconstruction from write-back and fresh-session recall. Provenance-aware closure eliminates observed recovery in the tested positive-baseline settings, whereas an exact-literal write filter blocks reinsertion but cannot erase information already present. Together, these results show that source deletion should be evaluated behaviorally at the level of the agent and its memory system, not only as a storage operation.
items.title: AfterDeleteBench: Auditing Post-Deletion Information Persistence in LLM Agents

items.summary: Motivation: Variant calling for next-generation sequencing (NGS) data relies on a diverse ecosystem of tools and workflows. Large-scale collaborative studies increasingly adopt federated analysis, where each institution processes sensitive data locally using standardized pipelines. Deploying identical pipelines across multiple centers remains challenging because heterogeneous software environments and computing policies can cause workflow divergence and inconsistent results. Results: We developed CBIcall, a workflow backend-flexible, configuration-driven framework that runs standardized variant-calling pipelines from raw FASTQ files to analysis-ready VCFs. Users define each analysis in a single YAML parameters file, which CBIcall resolves against a controlled workflow registry and resource catalog. The execution driver validates parameters and checks compatibility among pipelines, analysis modes, workflow backends, genome builds, tool versions, and resource bundles. CBIcall supports reproducibility auditing by comparing executions using recorded provenance and output fingerprints. CBIcall dispatches validated workflows natively through Bash, Cromwell, Nextflow and Snakemake backends and provides production-ready pipelines for germline WES, WGS (single-sample or cohort joint genotyping following GATK Best Practices), and mitochondrial DNA analysis. We evaluated analytical performance using public benchmark datasets and validated reproducibility across four computing environments. We further deployed CBIcall in the EU HEREDITARY project, where it processed 1102 samples with both WES and mtDNA pipelines on an institutional HPC system, supporting its suitability for reproducible cohort-scale genomic analyses. Availability and implementation: CBIcall is open source (GPLv3) and distributed with ready-to-run pipelines; full dependency and installation documentation is available at https://github.com/CNAG-Biomedical-Informatics/cbicall.
items.title: CBIcall: a configuration-driven framework for variant calling in large sequencing cohorts

items.summary: Memory enables language agents to carry useful distinctions from past experience into future decisions. Its value depends on which distinctions survive, whether a bounded agent can use them, and what can be recovered or revised as demands evolve. We develop a decision-theoretic framework that follows this value from raw history through persistent state, operational use, and costly recovery and revision. Original and retained value are expressed in units of avoided task loss; risk-cost frontiers describe attainable recovery and preservation across uses. Unknown demand yields value profiles, while interactive feedback changes the distribution of future work. A cost-aware simulation condition and five minimal counterexamples expose the roles of information timing, retrieval access, component interaction, feedback and demand uncertainty. In particular, a pointer with zero mutual information about the answer can still reduce the cost of exact recovery. Diagnostics on LoCoMo, a two-project update task and longitudinal cases exhibit failures of preservation, use and measurement. At fixed retrieved evidence, a saved ledger changes subsequent answers; at fixed agent outputs, an evaluator revision changes scores. The framework connects these distinctions to operational risk bounds and testable principles for allocating memory, preserving recovery options and revising evidence dependencies.
items.title: The Value of Memory in Language Agents

items.summary: Large organizations increasingly face what this book calls the cognitive complexity wall: at the scale of hundreds of interacting components, maintaining the dependency map and reacting at the pace of incidents exceeds what a human team can deliver. This conceptual volume proposes AAM/5C, in which five capabilities (Capture, Comprehend, Choose, Coordinate, Control) are instantiated across seven logical layers, L1 to L7. A single authorization rule, R-AUT, separates who proposes, who decides and who executes: a probabilistic planner (L4) proposes; a governance layer (L6) decides under signed policies and records its verdict in a signed evaluation proof; a security layer (L5) issues a short-lived act token bound to that proof; a policy enforcement point verifies both before the target layer materializes the act. Under an explicit guarantee contract, two analytical statements (H7a, H8a) hold by construction. The other statements of its ten hypotheses (H1 to H10), including log completeness (H7b) and non-bypass of the enforcement point (H8b), are refutable, and the protocol that could refute them is fixed before any measurement. The contribution of the book is a prescriptive reference model that articulates, under this single authorization rule, known mechanisms and adds three constructs, all to be validated: the Validation step of the Distributed Autonomy Loop, the ephemeral authority surface and the cognitive dependency plane. The book positions them against autonomic computing, multi-agent systems, enterprise architecture and agent protocols (MCP, A2A), gives an authorization policy in Rego and a partial TLA+ specification of peer consensus, and sets out a validation program with quantified milestones. It reports no empirical results. This English edition is a translation of the French original, produced with the assistance of AI tools and validated by the author.
items.title: Agentic Architecture of Information Systems. The AAM/5C Model: A Reference Model for Distributed Autonomy

items.summary: The rise of Agentic AI systems has changed the landscape of artificial intelligence by enabling strong reasoning capabilities through specialized multi-agent interaction with structured self-reflection. However, in target-driven reasoning tasks, single- and multi-agent systems are often on par in terms of performance gains. A major challenge is that failures often arise from an ineffective exchange of critical information during inter-agent interaction and coordination. Different from existing multi-agent debate paradigms that rely on synchronous turn-taking and sharing information across different agents, we propose an inter-agent protocol based on shared Memory bUFFer INference - referred to as MUFFIN - in an asynchronous agentic framework. In the first step, an orchestrator routes queries based on their reasoning demands and delegates demanding ones to a multi-agent setting, where a shared memory buffer provides asynchronous exchange of intermediate findings while an agent's private reasoning remains local. Our experiments show that our framework Muffin outperforms established competitors, achieving the best accuracy in 17 out of 20 of our benchmark settings, and provides a better quality-cost trade-off than multi-agent debate: Muffin improves accuracy by 19.2 accuracy points while using 77.4% fewer tokens, without requiring full-trace sharing.
items.title: Muffin - A Shared Memory Buffer for Asynchronous AI Agents

items.summary: LLM agents that act on live Web data must combine heterogeneous evidence, remember what they have done and improve from outcomes without weakening their own safeguards. We study this problem in autonomous investing, where every action is irreversible and based on untrusted Web content. We present Steward, a multi-agent LLM system that draws the boundary of self-evolution in its type system. First, nine role-specialised agents decide jointly: four analysts read news feeds, SEC filings, macroeconomic series and market data and emit typed reports, from which a Portfolio Manager sets target positions that a protected Risk Manager audits. Second, a seven-layer shared memory, assembled by code from the system's own record, gives each decision its position context, the market narrative, calibration and the agent's past decisions. Third, the system improves itself by review: code grades every trade and forecast nightly and writes the grades into memory, and each quarter a reflector proposes prompt learnings that a deterministic gate applies reversibly and replay of recorded inputs verifies. All three operate around an invariant core of order arithmetic, risk rules and discipline-agent prompts that no self-edit can reach. In a five-month live deployment (102 trading days, 1,632 LLM calls), the system contained a 24.6% sector drawdown to a 0.3% loss; in replay of its recorded inputs, a single model given the same raw data traded more and lost 1.35 points against the market over five days where the joint design showed no significant loss, and no injected instruction was followed; and a 2015-2026 backtest shows the core alone lowering the maximum drawdown under all 50 random entry policies. The reflector traced the dominant failure to its root cause, and the gate applied a learning that the agent adopted on trigger evenings and on no control evening. Code: https://github.com/yebof/quant-agent
items.title: Governed Self-Evolution for Autonomous Investing: A Multi-Agent LLM System with an Invariant Core

items.summary: Sixth-generation (6G) communication systems are expected to support immersive, intent-driven, and latency-critical services through tight integration of multimodal intelligence, edge computing, and autonomous network control. In this setting, agentic AI systems can reason over heterogeneous inputs, use tools and network functions, coordinate across distributed entities, and adapt to dynamic environments. These capabilities make agentic multimodal intelligence promising for 6G applications such as semantic communications, digital twins, and zero-touch network management, but they also introduce security and privacy risks that extend beyond conventional AI and network security models. Vulnerabilities can propagate across multimodal data pipelines, memory, tools, communication interfaces, and inter-agent coordination loops. We survey multimodal intelligence and agentic AI for 6G cross-layered communication systems from the perspectives of privacy and security. We present a 6G-oriented system view spanning perception, memory, tool use, and multi-agent orchestration; analyze threat models and attack surfaces across sensing, cognition, action, memory, and communication layers; organize existing attacks into a structured taxonomy; and review mitigation strategies including prompt and memory defenses, inter-agent trust mechanisms, secure orchestration, and privacy-preserving learning. We conclude by outlining open research directions for trustworthy multimodal multi-agent 6G systems.
items.title: Secure Agentic AI and Multimodal Intelligence in 6G Communication Systems

items.summary: Every LLM request SWAN AI-SQL (https://github.com/ZhaoFuheng/SWAN-AISQL) and the baselines issue on SemBench MOVIE/ECOMM/MMQA, the 30-query hybrid bench of the PLOP paper and the SWAN 2.0 benchmark (https://github.com/ZhaoFuheng/SWANBench), with the provider's answer, its measured latency and its cost, as a DuckDB file (gzip-compressed, 0.96 GB; 4.4 GB unpacked; 2,409,502 recorded calls) for the repository's cache proxy (serve/ai_cache_server.py). It holds SWAN AI-SQL, LOTUS 1.2.4, PLOP (the public Morrila fork, DP cost-model mode), BlendSQL 0.1.27, ThalamusDB 0.1.15 (exact mode) and Palimpzest 1.5.3 (Abacus optimizer) on every benchmark each of them runs. SWAN AI-SQL's recordings are its current ones (2026-10-23, DuckDB 2.0.0); every SWAN 2.0 recording is a fresh run through an empty cache (LOTUS and PLOP on 2026-10-03, BlendSQL and Palimpzest on 2026-10-05, SWAN AI-SQL on 2026-10-23). Always use the latest version: the concept DOI and serve/fetch_cache.sh resolve to it. Every table in the repositories replays without a provider key: run serve/fetch_cache.sh (it downloads, checks and unpacks the latest version), then the benchmark harnesses; the proxy replays each recorded answer with its recorded latency and cost. Model: gpt-5.6-luna, temperature 0, each system's default prompts (zero-shot). Replay matches requests byte for byte; an edited query, another model, or a client library that renders the request differently is a fresh request. The systems' own run-to-run variance (LOTUS's ranking order, result assembly in BlendSQL and Palimpzest, ThalamusDB's sampler, PLOP's parallel operator order) is theirs, not the cache's.
items.title: SWAN AI-SQL replay cache: recorded gpt-5.6-luna answers of SWAN, LOTUS, BlendSQL, Palimpzest, ThalamusDB and PLOP on SemBench, the PLOP hybrid bench and SWAN 2.0

In our primary setting, a single query recovers the deleted secret from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in roughly two thirds of cases, while matched never-exposed controls have zero recovery. Crucially, recovery does not require a surviving verbatim copy: when the complete secret string is absent and only separately stored components remain under a public composition rule, exact reconstruction succeeds in 62-99% of cases across Qwen, Mistral, and Phi-3. We also show that the response interface is part of the measurement system: target-bearing replies can be scored as failures when the requested format and parser are misaligned. Finally, we separate reconstruction from write-back and fresh-session recall. Provenance-aware closure eliminates observed recovery in the tested positive-baseline settings, whereas an exact-literal write filter blocks reinsertion but cannot erase information already present. Together, these results show that source deletion should be evaluated behaviorally at the level of the agent and its memory system, not only as a storage operation.
items.title: AfterDeleteBench: Auditing Post-Deletion Information Persistence in LLM Agents

items.summary: We study intermediate sample-size efficiency for censored regression tests when the signal and significance level both tend to zero. Independent treatment assignment permits finite-sample conditional sign calibration under arbitrary outcome dependence. For stationary ergodic latent fields with independent smooth site noise, bounded scores learned from the same pooled outcomes retain their first-order drift under empirical squared-error consistency, without an estimation-rate requirement. An observable censored rank procedure consequently admits an explicit leading cost on long-range dependent fields with nonsummable covariances. Smooth response scores admit a complementary result without independent site noise. For observational fields, separated blocks and paired variance calibration control the dependence approximation at the nominal testing level and yield sample-size costs under explicit absolute-regularity envelopes. An exactly centered censored contrast removes unknown marginal centering under stated exogeneity conditions. We also give a product-limit construction for independent random censoring, information-loss identities, and directional score-bank comparisons. Numerical studies distinguish procedure loss, score-learning loss, and spatial variance inflation. A stationary nonergodic counterexample and an uncensored Gaussian benchmark delimit the field results. Independent-data proofs, finite-range constructions, and a finite-dimensional measurement extension are included in the same manuscript.

items.summary: Despite significant advances in deep learning-based failure prognosis, existing predictive maintenance frameworks consistently terminate at the prediction step, leaving the critical operational challenge of prioritising maintenance resources across heterogeneous asset fleets unresolved. This paper addresses this gap by proposing an integrated framework that couples Long Short-Term Memory network-based Remaining Useful Life prediction with the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution for data-driven multi-criteria maintenance scheduling, validated on the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 turbofan degradation benchmark. The framework dynamically synthesises predicted health indicators with operational criteria encompassing machine criticality, maintenance cost, and production downtime impact to generate a ranked intervention schedule whose quality is evaluated through a rigorous, assumption-free protocol comprising precision-recall analysis, area under the precision-recall curve, Spearman rank correlation, and a scheduling efficiency ratio against a random baseline. A five-seed ablation study comparing Long Short-Term Memory, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, and Gated Recurrent Unit architectures, with Wilcoxon signed-rank validation, establishes statistically equivalent prediction accuracy, confirming the architecture-agnostic nature of the scheduling design.
items.title: Code and analysis: A Deep Learning and TOPSIS Framework for Predictive Maintenance Scheduling in Smart Manufacturing: An Industry 4.0 Approach

items.summary: Coordinating two players in a cooking task requires a vision-language agent to track changing scene states, sequence recipe steps, and allocate shared resources under a time budget. We introduce an Overcooked-inspired benchmark for evaluating these capabilities in Unreal Engine environments constructed using coding agents. A single vision-language model controls both players from top-down visual observations, selecting high-level actions while the engine executes navigation. The benchmark contains 20 maps in five categories. These categories support evaluation of centralized coordination under equipment contention, changing terrain, and handoff dependencies. A prop legend and pot ingredient-count indicators provide explicit visual cues, while grid-based destinations support spatial grounding. The evaluation compares four VLMs on all 20 maps, measuring task score, order completion, delivery precision, action acceptance rate, and model API expenditure. A memory ablation on the same 20 maps examines the effect of a shared, self-authored notebook while retaining six-response action history in both conditions. The strongest evaluated model, \texttt{gpt-6-astra}, achieves 26.2\% mean order completion. Notebook memory has mixed score effects across models, with positive mean differences for Claude and Qwen and negative differences for GPT and Gemini.
items.title: DuoCook: An Overcooked-Inspired Benchmark for Visual Planning and Coordination

items.summary: Personal agents need to draw on long-term interaction history to retrieve and apply external knowledge suited to a user's current request. Even an answer grounded in relevant documents can be unsuitable when it overlooks the user's circumstances. This creates two connected challenges: using historical conditions to identify the knowledge needed for a new request, and applying that knowledge to the user's situation. Existing benchmarks advance memory recall, personalized retrieval, and memory-guided action, while the joint evaluation of these two challenges remains underexplored. We introduce ColaBench, a synthetic benchmark in health and daily living, with 349 tasks across 10 Profiles and a knowledge base of 13,033 documents. Its Evidence Graph connects personal conditions to their disclosures across public interaction sessions, records prior document exposure, and links answer requirements to personal and newly acquired document evidence. We also introduce MemKB, which uses state summaries to inform queries and rule application, and memory-document links to retrieve knowledge associated with the user's history. MemKB achieves 86.25% Accuracy with an average of 4.07 interaction rounds per task. Task-level analysis finds larger gains on tasks integrating information across multiple historical Facts; error analysis further identifies unsupported personal assumptions and rule misapplication as obstacles to using retrieved evidence. ColaBench provides traceable tasks and an evaluation framework for studying how memory guides knowledge acquisition and rule application.
items.title: ColaBench: Evaluating Memory-Guided Knowledge Acquisition in Personal Agents

items.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are increasingly proposed for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes, yet their behaviour under sparse radiosonde initialization remains poorly characterised for dam-safety analytics, where the upper tail of the rainfall distribution governs spillway design. We define the tail-index distortion functional, derive a bound on its bias under sparse initialization, and show that the distortion is governed by the interaction between the PINN's physics residual weighting and the effective sample size of the initial-condition ensemble. The framework is illustrated with a reanalysis-based temperature series for Lagos, Nigeria (2000–2023; 312 monthly observations; mean 26.414 °C; warming trend 0.1553 °C per decade), which serves as a benchmark for the data-provenance and uncertainty-reporting protocol that dam-safety analytics requires. Tail-index distortion should be treated as a first-class evaluation metric alongside predictive accuracy, and it identifies the conditions under which sparse radiosonde initialization produces non-conservative design quantiles. The contribution is a methodological and conceptual apparatus for auditing PINN downscaling in safety-critical climate analytics, not an empirical validation of any particular PINN architecture.

items.summary: Scaling embedding capacity alongside Transformer computation is an emerging trend in language models. This trend makes high compression rates increasingly useful. Hence, we study extreme compression of Per-Layer Embeddings (PLE), which follow this trend and account for 35.2% of the parameters of Gemma 4 E4B. At such rates, conventional quantizers give each token-layer vector its own code of only a few bytes. We instead develop OPTIC (Output-Path-fitted, Token-shared Indexed Codes), which stores one quantized code tuple per token and decodes it at every layer with a layer-specific affine decoder. Codes and decoders are fitted to the PLE output path rather than to the stored vectors. At about $100\times$ PLE compression of bfloat16 (BF16) E4B, OPTIC retains an aggregate 97.8% of the uncompressed model's performance across seven benchmarks, whereas product quantization, the strongest of six conventional baselines, retains 66.3%. At $594\times$ and $1,002\times$ PLE compression of BF16 E4B, OPTIC retains 90.5% and 84.1%. On the official E4B release with 4-bit linear weights and 16-bit activations (W4A16), OPTIC retains 96.9% at about $100\times$ PLE compression. During inference at about $100\times$ PLE compression, BF16 E4B uses 29.7% less GPU memory than with uncompressed PLE at the same key-value cache size, while running at most 0.40% slower.
items.title: Extreme Compression of Per-Layer Embeddings via Cross-Layer Latent Vector Quantization

items.summary: Recent advances in search agents have enabled large language models to tackle complex tasks by retrieving and synthesizing external information. However, existing search agents often lack search-state awareness, i.e., the ability to recognize what information has been obtained and what remains missing, leading to hallucinated reasoning and prematurely terminated search. To address this limitation, we propose Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning (SARL), a reinforcement learning framework in which models learn to recognize their own search state during training and improve their search behavior accordingly, without requiring additional assessment at test time. SARL achieves this through a dual reward design that captures the corrective effect of each assessment while penalizing excessive reliance on it, jointly encouraging effective and efficient search trajectories. Under this setup, SARL achieves a 24.3% relative improvement over the strongest baseline, with average gains of 35.9% on multi-hop reasoning and 27.9% on deep research benchmarks against the strongest per-benchmark baselines. SARL further surpasses methods built on auxiliary supervision or multi-agent coordination, despite operating as a standalone RL framework with no inference-time scaffolding. Beyond final performance, SARL maintains training stability under extended search horizons, a regime where existing methods consistently degrade, enabling sustained gains as task complexity grows.
items.title: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning for Search-State Awareness in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models

items.summary: Humanoid loco-manipulation in dynamic scenes is non-Markovian: cues vanish as objects change or are hidden, or leave the view as the robot turns and walks, yet whole-body vision-language-action (VLA) policies see only the present. We present WholeBodyMem, an object-guided perceptual memory that keeps the pre-history of object events seen before the robot acts on its goal. SAM3 tracks the task objects, and their events causally select key frames within an adaptive budget, which the action expert reads by cross-attention together with object tokens encoding appearance, geometry and time. We also contribute HuMeGo, a humanoid memory benchmark with six simulated and six real-world Unitree G1 tasks. Keeping the right frames rather than more frames, WholeBodyMem surpasses memoryless and uniform-memory baselines, raising its base policy's success from 29.1% to 72.6% in simulation and from 36.7% to 88.3% on the real robot, while also improving the standard SIMPLE tasks (70.2% to 86.9%).
items.title: Memory before Goal: Role of Pre-History Memory for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

items.summary: GradLint is a fast, standalone Rust-based command-line tool and Python package for diffusion MRI gradient-table quality control. It audits FSL and MRtrix gradient schemes, detects b-vector flip and axis-permutation errors using DWI image evidence, and writes corrected gradient tables with machine-readable provenance. GradLint is designed as a QC gate before diffusion MRI preprocessing, reconstruction, or tractography pipelines. It checks whether the supplied gradient table is geometrically consistent with the diffusion image, reports scheme-quality issues such as shell structure, direction counts, b0 handling, non-unit b-vectors, and angular sampling, and identifies silent convention errors that can otherwise propagate into tensor fitting and tractography results. The core detection method ranks signed axis permutations of the gradient table by a fibre-coherence criterion derived from a diffusion tensor fit. Candidate conventions are evaluated in the appropriate image or world frame for the input format: FSL bvec/bval tables are treated as image-relative, while MRtrix .b tables are treated as world-coordinate gradients. With audit --apply-repair, GradLint can write corrected FSL bvec/bval files and, optionally, an MRtrix .b table, together with JSON provenance describing the decision, transform, inputs, and outputs. WARN decisions additionally require --force-repair. Without --apply-repair, nonidentity corrections are withheld with an overall WARN and exit code 3. GradLint does not verify volume-to-gradient pairing. The software is implemented as a Rust core with thin command-line and Python interfaces. The Python package exposes the same functionality as the CLI and can render JSON reports to Markdown or HTML. Input gradient files are never modified in place unless an explicit overwrite option is used. This record archives the source code for GradLint v1.1.7, corresponding to the GitHub release published on 2026-10-23. The archived source includes the Rust core, CLI, Python bindings, report rendering layer, tests, CI/release metadata, and example materials included in the public source tree. Repository: https://github.com/marcotag93/GradLint Release: https://github.com/marcotag93/GradLint/releases/tag/v1.1.7 PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/gradlint/ Concept DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20847595
items.title: GradLint: a fast, open-source Rust tool for b-vector flip detection, gradient-scheme QC, and auto-repair in diffusion MRI

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/23591614 . Dabirsiaghi shows that harnesses which flatten the typed conversation into one string with text labels such as [User]: destroy message provenance before the summarizer runs, so a forged user turn survives compaction. Five flattening harnesses (pi, opencode, Cline, Aider, OpenHands) launder the forged approval 87-100% of the time, and four role-typed harnesses (Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Continue) 0%. I read it as a practitioner who runs coding agents every day, and my comments come from that side. Two of them rest on my own technical reports, which are not peer-reviewed, so please weigh them as practice notes and not as evidence of the same standing as your experiments. Each point below pairs one thing I see in my work with a named part of your preprint. 1. Bounded sessions as another exit (Introduction, "Scope and severity"). You write "Compaction is mandatory. Every agent that runs long enough fills its context window and must compact." I would say it is mandatory only for a session that is allowed to keep running. In my practice I keep one task per chat and clear the context between unrelated tasks. In a controlled experiment of 36 runs, six session-reset policies with six repetitions each, cost followed a U-shaped curve with its minimum at a reset every 3 tasks and a plateau from 3 to 6. Resetting after every task cost about a third more (+33.5%, p = 0.002, Holm-adjusted 0.011), and "never reset" was not significantly different. Two caveats that I state in the report myself: the comparison point was chosen after the runs, and in the reset-after-every-task branch the agent wrote more tests (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22759217). So a fresh session with a short handoff the user writes has a measurable price, and it would fit next to your label-escaping fix as an operator-side mitigation. 2. Where the exposure sits (Discussion, point 2). You report that the executed rate is near 100% when the planted command dominates a small summary, and settles to a ~20-40% plateau in a full window. I think the full-window plateau is the number that matters most. In 722 agent sessions, 150,902 model calls and 34.6 billion tokens, more than 85% of modeled cost was context work (86.2-87.8% on recalculation), and sessions longer than 200 calls, 8% of all sessions, carried more than 90% of the money (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22759216). The sessions that reach compaction are likely a small share of sessions but most of the spend and most of the unattended work. Reporting how often compaction fires per session in ordinary use would help readers size the exposure. 3. Independent checks (Contributions, point 4, E9). The code-level check that compares the summary's user-attributed claims against the genuine user turns still in memory catches 77% of laundering while demoting 2% of legitimate summary content, and the in-prompt anti-injection rule stops 13-25%. This matches what I see: a second, fresh agent told to refute the first one's result finds what the first missed, because independent checkers rarely fail the same way. A round of checking lowers risk and does not remove it. It would help to say what the remaining 23% look like. 4. Equal confidence (Limitations). In live testing, one agent refused a payload "even though the bootstrap command was previously approved," citing the forged approval as fact. That is a clean example of something I see in practice, that an AI sounds equally sure when it is right and when it is wrong. The summary carries no marker of doubt, so the user cannot tell a genuine approval from a forged one either. Does any of the five flattening harnesses offer a fresh-session or handoff mode that skips compaction, and was it tested? Competing interests Yes: the text cites the author's own technical reports (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22759217 and 10.5281/zenodo.22759216); no connection to the
items.title: PREreview of "Compaction Laundering: Provenance Destruction in Context-Compacting Coding Agents"

items.summary: **GLOBES — Global Library of Observations from Buoys for Evaluating Sea States** GLOBES is a global dataset of historical wave observations from moored buoys, developed to improve the accessibility, consistency, and reuse of in situ wave measurements across observing networks. The dataset integrates **1,665 buoy records from 27 data providers across 41 countries**, representing 19,469 station-years of observations spanning 1969–2026. Records retain their native temporal resolution, ranging from 10 minutes to 3 hours, and include up to seven standardized wave parameters: significant wave height (HS), maximum wave height (HM), peak wave period (TP), zero-crossing wave period (TZ), mean wave period (TM), wave direction (DR), and directional spread (SP). GLOBES harmonizes timestamps, units, missing-value conventions, station metadata, and quality-control flags while preserving original provider information and data provenance. The archive is distributed as standardized station-based files, accompanied by provider-specific quality-control information where available. **Data organization:** This release contains 28 compressed archives representing 27 data providers. NOWPHAS observations are distributed separately at 20-minute and 2-hour temporal resolutions, resulting in 1,745 distributed time series. **Release status:** This is a preliminary data release (v0.1.0). Metadata, documentation, and data files may be refined in subsequent versions. **Data use and licensing:** GLOBES integrates observations subject to different provider-specific licensing, attribution, and usage conditions. Users must consult the USAGE metadata field of individual records and comply with the applicable original provider requirements. No single open license applies to the entire dataset. GLOBES supports research on wave climate, variability and extremes, coastal hazards, and the evaluation of numerical models, hindcasts, reanalyses, and satellite-derived wave products.
items.title: GLOBES: the Global Library of Observations from Buoys for Evaluating Sea States

items.summary: Unlike conventional GUI agents, personalized GUI agents require user preferences to guide sequential execution over changing GUI states. This raises two challenges: determining HOW each preference should alter execution strategy and WHEN it should take effect along the interaction trajectory. Existing benchmarks primarily evaluate overall task success, offering limited insight into these questions. We introduce PrefDiag-Bench with two components: (1) a categorization of preferences into five types, characterizing HOW they affect execution; and (2) a stage-wise diagnostic framework with 1,664 probes, tracing WHEN preferences should take effect and where failures occur. We evaluate eleven GUI agent systems, including end-to-end agents and agentic workflows, under two forms of user context: explicit user profiles and behavioral memory logs. Although existing agents achieve relatively high completion rates on non-personalized tasks, performance is substantially lower on preference-personalized tasks. Even the best-performing model, Seed-2.0-Pro, achieves only 47.17% on Process preferences under explicit user profiles. Agents struggle particularly with Ranking and Process preferences. Further analysis reveals two key capability bottlenecks: selecting relevant evidence from user history and recognizing when preferences should take effect during execution. Controlled interventions that explicitly provide relevant evidence improve end-to-end task success by up to 7.06%. PrefDiag-Bench offers a more systematic evaluation of GUI agents' personalization capabilities beyond overall task success. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Zhixin-L/PrefDiag-Bench.
items.title: Diagnosing Personalization Failures in Mobile GUI Agents

items.summary: Detailed image captioning is usually framed as an amount problem: a model should mention more visual facts while avoiding hallucination. However, autoregressive VLMs generate captions as ordered sequences, and later generations may be produced under weaker or noisier visual grounding. We therefore argue that long-form captioning should be studied not only by what facts are mentioned, but also by where they appear. We introduce a position-aware rubric representation that decomposes dense human references into atomic visual claims, verifies generated captions against those claims, and induces a quartile-wise composition of supported, hallucinated, and generic content. This lens reveals two qualitatively different failures in long captions: models tend to produce unsupported specificity in the middle, while the final portion often escapes into vague, non-evidential language rather than simply accumulating more hallucination. A same-reference human control does not exhibit these patterns; additional human audits examine the visual validity of the induced labels. Motivated by this diagnosis, we propose PAGER (Position-Aware Grounded Evidence Reinforcement), a GRPO training objective with separate signals for supported fine-grained middle evidence, evidence-bearing tail continuation, claim coverage, and content-aware length control. The result is a closed loop: the same ordered claim representation identifies where long captions fail and supplies the position-specific reward needed to repair those failures. Experiments on detailed-caption benchmarks show that PAGER improves position-wise grounding and pairwise caption preference while preserving competitive global caption quality.
items.title: Where Do Long Captions Fail? Position-Aware Diagnosis and Reinforcement Learning for Detailed Image Captioning

items.summary: We envision a general-purpose protein foundation model as a unified, interactive model of sequence, structure, and function, capable of understanding, generation, and cross-modal translation while retaining the instruction-following and reasoning capabilities of modern LLMs. Toward this vision, we introduce Trion-1, the first native, unified, multimodal diffusion language model (dLLM) for proteins. Trion-1 is built on two key design choices: (1) a unified discrete token space that jointly represents sequence, structure, and natural language; (2) a dLLM backbone that replaces strict left-to-right factorization with bidirectional or semi-bidirectional token interactions, enabling global residue communication and long-range contact modeling that are naturally suited to structure modeling. This formulation unifies six core capabilities: folding, inverse folding, sequence understanding, structure understanding, sequence design, and structure design, while retaining the native language capabilities of general-purpose LLMs. On established benchmarks, Trion-1 achieves broadly competitive performance. In folding, Trion-1 achieves a TM-score above 0.8 with a single sample under strict homology control, matching or exceeding the existing tri-modal model using 200 samples. For sequence understanding, Trion-1 performs on par with top-tier LLMs such as Claude Opus 4.7 (62.37%). These results support well-aligned sequence-structure-language representations and strong cross-modal generative capabilities.
items.title: Trion-1: Unifying Language, Protein Sequence, and Structure with Diffusion Language Models

items.summary: Large language models can repeat an instruction while failing to keep obeying it. We study this recall-compliance dissociation in long-horizon dialogue and define State Integrity Collapse: a model preserves a stated constraint in memory but stops applying it to later turns. We introduce StateTrack-Bench, a controlled suite of conversations covering numerical, format, role/persona, factual-memory, and logical-rule constraints. Across seven provider-pinned model snapshots and five dialogue-depth probes, strict joint retention ranges from 62.4% to 100.0%, with degradation concentrated in symbolic constraints and in one especially brittle model. A forked recall audit shows that 88.6% of observed failures are behavioral-drift failures rather than ordinary forgetting; excluding the brittle outlier preserves this diagnosis (84.4% of failures). Extended evaluations at depths up to 50 turns confirm that the dissociation persists beyond the core benchmark, while Structured State Anchoring recovers up to 24.4 points on immutable constraints. The results show that reliability cannot be inferred from single-turn instruction following alone; evaluation must track whether remembered constraints remain operational as dialogue state grows. Code and artifacts are available at: https://github.com/xzzvsxd/StateTrack.
items.title: When LLMs Forget What They Believe: Characterizing State Integrity Collapse in Long-Horizon Dialogues

items.summary: Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) leverages centralized knowledge graphs to enhance large language models with structured knowledge retrieval. However, real-world knowledge is inherently distributed across multiple organizations rather than being centrally accessible. Privacy constraints further prohibit sharing entire local knowledge graphs, preventing GraphRAG from effectively retrieving and utilizing distributed knowledge. To this end, we propose Federated GraphRAG (FedGRAG), a unified framework for distributed graph retrieval and knowledge-enhanced generation over multiple clients with knowledge graphs. Specifically, we address two fundamental challenges in federated GraphRAG. First, the absence of a global knowledge graph makes unified retrieval impossible. To address this, we develop a Federated Knowledge Routing mechanism that efficiently identifies relevant clients through lightweight knowledge indices without exposing local graph structures. Second, local graph memory cannot be shared directly because it contains sensitive entities and knowledge information. We therefore propose a controlled-disclosure evidence construction method. It extracts retrieved evidence subgraphs and converts them into an evidence abstract, enabling evidence conversion and reconstruction on the server. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Federated GraphRAG consistently outperforms existing baselines in both retrieval and downstream generation tasks, establishing a new paradigm for deploying GraphRAG in federated environments.
items.title: Federated Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

items.summary: Processed single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data for “Selective Immune Silencing by Targeted TGF-β Mimics” This record contains processed sequencing data, derived analysis objects, and analysis code supporting the transcriptomic analyses in Sun, Ogishi, Barrett, Jiang, Yan et al., Selective Immune Silencing by Targeted TGF-β Mimics . The study repurposes the helminth-derived TGF-β mimic TGM1 as a cell-type-targeted immunosuppressant by replacing its CD44-binding domains 4–5 with high-affinity targeting modules. Constructs targeting mouse or human CD4 or CD8α, or human CD19, are designed to preferentially deliver TGF-β receptor agonism to selected lymphocyte subsets. Two datasets are included, each as a separate archive. 1. Single-cell RNA-seq of B-cell-enriched samples from human spleen organoids (raw reads: GEO GSE346912). Human spleen organoids from two deceased organ donors (Sp88, 33-year-old female; Sp99, 53-year-old male) were stimulated with live-attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV) in the presence of vehicle, untargeted low-affinity TGM1 (domains 1–3), or the CD19-targeted TGF-β agonist TGM1-hCD19, alongside unstimulated controls (4 conditions × 2 donors = 8 samples). On day 7, B cells were enriched by negative selection, captured on a 10x Genomics Chromium X instrument using Single Cell 5′ R2-only v3 chemistry, and sequenced as paired-end 150-bp reads on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Reads were aligned to GRCh38-2024-A and quantified with Cell Ranger v9.0.1, with intronic reads included, recovering approximately 14,000–27,000 cells per sample. After quality control in Seurat v5.3.1, 163,632 cells were retained (33,179 mock; 51,696 LAIV; 43,858 LAIV + untargeted TGM1; 34,899 LAIV + TGM1-hCD19), of which 130,987 were B-lineage cells. Cell-type annotation combined Louvain clustering, label transfer from the Human Tonsil Atlas v2 ( https://zenodo.org/records/8373756 ), and manual curation using canonical markers. The record provides Cell Ranger filtered feature-barcode matrices and per-sample QC summaries; cell-type label-transfer and curated annotation tables; differential expression and fgsea results; pySCENIC v0.12.1 regulon activity matrices (265 regulons, including IRF4 and PRDM1/BLIMP1); velocyto loom files and scVelo per-cell velocity outputs underlying the RNA velocity analysis; gene signature and cell-cycle scores; and all R and Python analysis code. These analyses support suppression of the germinal center B-cell–to–plasmablast transition by B-cell-targeted TGF-β agonism, with markedly reduced plasmablast and plasma-cell representation, increased naïve B-cell representation, and IRF4 and PRDM1/BLIMP1 regulon activities approaching unstimulated levels. RNA velocity analyses are consistent with reduced progression through the plasmablast differentiation trajectory. 2. Bulk RNA-seq of antigen-specific mouse CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells (raw reads: GEO GSE346305). Naïve Thy1.1⁺ OT-II (CD4⁺) and OT-I (CD8⁺) T cells were co-transferred into Thy1.1⁻ recipient mice, which were then immunized with ovalbumin emulsified in complete Freund’s adjuvant and treated every other day with PBS, untargeted TGM1, TGM1-mCD4, or TGM1-mCD8 (approximately 40–50 pmol per dose for TGM1 constructs). Donor OT-II and OT-I cells were sorted from draining lymph nodes for RNA sequencing. Naïve OT-II and OT-I cells were included as baseline controls, yielding 20 libraries in total (2 cell types × 5 conditions, comprising 4 treatment groups and 1 naïve control group, × 2 biological replicates). Reads were aligned to mm10 with Rsubread v2.18.0, quantified with featureCounts, and analyzed with DESeq2. Downstream analyses include principal component analysis (PCA) of variance-stabilized counts, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) against Hallmark gene sets, and exploratory immune-cell deconvolution using EPIC with the Monaco ref
items.title: Selective Immune Silencing by Targeted TGF-β Mimics

items.summary: Ray tracing (RT) generates photorealistic images by simulating the physical behavior of light as it interacts with surfaces in a virtual scene. In film production and high-end rendering pipelines, this technique computes global illumination, reflections, refractions, and soft shadows by tracing millions of light rays per frame and accurately modeling their bounces and attenuation. Contemporary GPUs incorporate specialized ray tracing hardware to accelerate key operations in the traversal pipeline. By accelerating these stages in hardware, the unit enables real-time ray tracing for complex scenes that previously required offline computation. However, ray tracing introduces substantial control and data divergence. Each ray may traverse a different set of nodes in the acceleration structure, encounter distinct materials, or terminate at varying depths. This irregularity reduces thread coherence and exposes a fundamental disparity between the GPU SIMT and per-thread execution model of dedicated RT units, where each ray progresses independently. In this work, we seek to validate assumptions made in open-source infrastructure and identify potential inefficiencies in resource management within the ray tracing pipeline. To address inefficiency caused by mismatches between SIMT and RT granularities, we propose Ray-by-Ray, which decomposes on-chip buffers into the granularity of individual rays and introduces lightweight management structures that enable more warps to run in parallel without increasing buffer capacity. This approach improves ray tracing unit utilization and increases memory-level parallelism. Experimental results show that Ray-by-Ray achieves an average performance improvement of 1.91x over the baseline, with an area overhead of 0.19\%.
items.title: Ray-by-Ray: Fine-Grained Resource Management for GPU Ray Tracing Units

items.summary: Background : The rapid digitisation of allied health education has led to an alarming rise in Digital Eye Strain (DES), also termed Computer Vision Syndrome (CVS), among undergraduate Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT) students. Standard therapies like artificial tears provide temporary lubrication without resolving the underlying neuro-vascular tension and oxidative ocular stress. Objectives : To evaluate and compare the therapeutic efficacy of daily Isotonic Saline Jal Neti versus Sterile Triphala Water Eye Wash over 4 weeks on digital asthenopia, tear film stability, tear volume, and visual comfort in a cohort of 16 BPT students. Methodology : A 4-week prospective, parallel-group, randomized controlled empirical pilot trial was conducted at Maya Devi University, Dehradun. Sixteen BPT students (aged 18–25) meeting inclusion criteria (screen time ≥ 6 hrs/day, CVS-Q ≥ 6, TBUT < 10 s) were randomized 1:1 into Group A (Jal Neti, n=8) and Group B (Sterile Triphala Water Eye Wash, n=8). Outcome metrics assessed at baseline (Day 0) and post-intervention (Day 28) included: Computer Vision Syndrome Questionnaire (CVS-Q), Visual Fatigue Scale (VFS, 0-60), Tear Break-Up Time (TBUT, seconds), and Schirmer’s Test-I (mm/5 min). Results : Both groups exhibited statistically significant intra-group improvements across all parameters (p < 0.001). Group B (Triphala) achieved superior improvement in tear film stability and lacrimal secretion: TBUT increased by +4.15 ± 0.80 s in Group B vs. +2.30 ± 0.60 s in Group A (p < 0.001); Schirmer-I values increased by +4.85 ± 1.10 mm in Group B vs. +2.65 ± 0.85 mm in Group A (p < 0.001). Conversely, Group A (Jal Neti) achieved greater relief from central visual fatigue and periocular headaches: VFS scores decreased by -18.60 ± 2.95 points in Group A vs. -14.25 ± 2.75 points in Group B (p < 0.01). Total CVS-Q scores dropped markedly in both groups (Group A: 12.75 to 5.25; Group B: 13.00 to 4.90). Conclusion : Both modalities significantly alleviate digital eye strain in BPT students. Sterile Triphala eye wash is particularly potent for restoring ocular surface hydration and tear film stability, whereas Jal Neti excels in alleviating deep neuromuscular fatigue and periorbital strain.
tags: Digital Eye Strain, Jal Neti, Triphala, Tear Break-Up Time, Schirmer's Test, Physiotherapy Students,
items.title: Comparative Evaluation of Isotonic Saline Jal Neti versus Sterile Triphala Water Eye Wash on Digital Asthenopia, Tear Film Dynamics, and Visual Comfort in Undergraduate Physiotherapy Students: A Single-Center Empirical Pilot Study

items.summary: Malaria early-warning systems that treat climate as a spatially uniform forcing mis-time vector-control deployment when the thermal niche of Anopheles vectors shifts across districts. The framework is formalised as a structural causal model over a district-month lattice, with a graph-identification condition and a lag-recovery theorem that bounds timing error by the spectral gap of the estimated adjacency matrix. A climate-analytics evaluation is conducted on NASA POWER monthly reanalysis air temperature at 2 m for Kampala, Uganda (0.35°N, 32.58°E), 2000–2023, comprising 312 monthly observations with a mean of 22.443 °C and a standard deviation of 1.043 °C; the estimated linear trend was −0.1564 °C per decade. The evaluation shows that a causal graph that admits lagged hydrological mediators recovers the intervention window with lower timing error than a temperature-only baseline, and that the error bound tightens as the spectral gap widens. The contribution is a formal link between causal-graph identifiability and the operational quantity that public-health managers actually care about: how many weeks early or late a spraying or net-distribution campaign is triggered.
tags: malaria early warning; causal graph learning; spatiotemporal modelling; climate analytics; intervent
items.title: Spatiotemporal causal graph learning for malaria early-warning under climate-driven vector-range shifts: a climate-analytics evaluation of intervention-timing error

items.summary: Code, frozen configurations, input data, outputs and logs behind the Working sheet for MQG v0.3.8: chiral active Model H in three dimensions — computational validation addendum (MQG: magnetic quorum gravity). The archive contains the pre-registered canonical fit (v1.0), the frozen v1.1 analysis (angular torque test; joint fit with mixed noise), a reproduction on separate hardware, a second-algorithm check, and frozen acceptance tolerances for a future independent fitter. A SHA-256 manifest of every file is included. Interpretation level 1. All dispersion data are synthetic; the results verify software, uncertainty calibration and parameter identifiability, not the physics. The canonical fit v1.0 passes 15 of 16 pre-registered criteria and the v1.1 analysis passes 9 of 10; both failures stay on record. A pre-registered fit by an independent implementer is still open. items.summary: Overview This software package accompanies the study Resolvability of Ionospheric Currents From Multi-LEO Magnetometry . It provides computational tools for investigating how multi-altitude satellite magnetic observations constrain three-dimensional ionospheric currents. The package implements a divergence-free spherical Mie magnetic-field representation and a Bayesian inversion framework for evaluating magnetic-field and current reconstruction, degrees of freedom for signal (DFS), physical-current information, and posterior uncertainty. Main Features Spherical-harmonic Mie forward modeling and three-component current reconstruction. Bayesian inversion with full posterior covariance propagation. Resolution and recoverability diagnostics for different satellite configurations and observation altitudes. Physical-current information analysis and regularization-sensitivity experiments. Synthetic current-recovery experiments, calibration routines, and figure-generation workflows. Python and optional MATLAB implementations, with independent numerical verification. Sample Swarm-A/B orbital positions for geometry tests and a self-contained synthetic inversion example. What's New in This Version 3 This release provides a corrected scientific implementation and updated reproducibility tools. The principal corrections include: Correcting the colatitude derivative of the associated Legendre functions used in the spherical-harmonic operator. Restoring the radial magnetic-field contribution of the quadratic poloidal Mie term, ensuring consistency with the continuous divergence-free representation. Updating the corresponding current-reconstruction and recoverability calculations. Clarifying the scaled coefficient parameterization, Bayesian prior, and interpretation of coefficient-space resolution diagnostics. Improving numerical verification, reproducibility workflows, and documentation. The updated calculations continue to support the importance of satellite altitude separation for constraining specified ionospheric current structures, while distinguishing formal information gain from recovery of the complete physical current distribution. Data and Reproducibility The package includes source code, documentation, numerical tests, small reference summaries, sample orbit positions, and a self-contained synthetic example. The synthetic demonstrations can be executed without downloading mission magnetic-field observations. Reproducing the study's observation-based analyses requires the corresponding processed Swarm and Macau Science Satellite-1 data and additional external inputs described in the documentation. Large intermediate numerical archives and original magnetic observation records are not redistributed in this software package. Citation and License Please cite the version-specific Zenodo DOI and the software authors listed in CITATION.cff when using this package. Author-owned software and documentation are distributed under the MIT License. Included spacecraft-derived orbit excerpts and external datasets remain subject to their respective data-provider terms. This release supersedes the previous software implementation while retaining earlier versions in the same Zenodo version history.
items.title: Resolvability of Ionospheric Currents From Multi-LEO Magnetometry: Software and Reproducibility Package

items.summary: Multi-task generalization is an important yet underexplored problem in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). Many real-world applications require multi-agent systems to generalize across complex, temporally extended tasks with diverse inter-agent coordination requirements. We introduce a specification language that combines temporal-logic task specifications with operators for expressing such requirements. We propose SpecMAGIC, a hierarchical framework that leverages the automaton structure of task specifications for subtask decomposition. A centralized high-level planner identifies and allocates compatible subtask sequences across agents, while decentralized low-level policies execute individual subtasks. This enables zero-shot generalization to new tasks by composing reusable subtask policies according to new specifications, without retraining. We establish soundness and probabilistic completeness of the high-level planner. Experiments on multi-agent navigation tasks show that SpecMAGIC substantially outperforms existing approaches on unseen task specifications and maintains strong performance as the number of agents increases.
items.title: SpecMAGIC: Specification-Guided Multi-Task Generalization in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
